source.title: Bitcoin Has Only Done This Twice Before. Here’s What Came Next
source.description:
Bitcoin just lost its 50-week moving average after five straight red weeks, reigniting fears that the Bitcoin bear market is back. But this rare post-bottom breakdown has happened only twice before, and what followed might surprise you. As Nvidia's AI selloff rattles Wall Street and pressure builds around Federal Reserve policy, inflation, and liquidity, is Bitcoin facing another leg down or the final shakeout before the next bull run?

after.text: We haven't done enough of the spending yet.
If there was a macro event which slowed down the demand side or something happened in the next couple years and these guys spent more and more money, I think it would be an issue.
But if we're all believing that they're not going to spend as much money for 2028, well, then that would mean that KEPX would probably be less next year.
They've already started on the stuff that will happen now.
If they're worried about 2028, maybe there'll be a delay, and that would be good for the bubble risk, meaning it would push out the buildout further and further, and that would be good.
Second thing is there'd be less capital needed.
That's put enormous pressure on rates to go higher.

Second thing is, if people believe that the market is going to go down and there's going to be less of a buildout and Brad Gerstner says this is 50 basis points off GDP, well, then that means that growth will come down, which means rates should come down.
So when you go through everything, a lot of those things were negatives for Bitcoin this year.
They were negatives for gold because they were all related to liquidity.
And I think the liquidity headwinds are going to drop off, and that's what I did in the video, to just highlight to people that maybe something good comes out of this for Bitcoin.
